summary: @c1-ease/core ships a postinstall and import-time beacon to a hardcoded VPS
details: The package has no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, and the package self-describes only as a 'Compatibility shim.' Its sole behavior is beacon.cjs, which collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), install path, process.cwd(), node/npm version, package name) and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). The beacon fires both at install time via scripts.postinstall and again at require time via a top-level call in index.js. The destination is an unbranded Contabo VPS unrelated to any declared publisher, and the @c1-ease scope plus hollow stub content are consistent with a dependency-confusion or typosquat probe whose only effect on the installer is unsolicited transmission of host-identifying data to an author-controlled server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
